sources.match: Computes the spinor norm image of the proper stabilizer of a nondyadic unimodular lattice of rank at least two and assembles the adelic spinor norm with unit components at almost all places.
The spinor norm of an integral element of SO over a local ring is a unit class, through GSpin.

nodes.title: Trace-even and trace-unimodular lattices over a totally real field
nodes.statement: Let F be a totally real number field with different 𝔡_F, (V, Q) a nondegenerate quadratic space over F with bilinear form (x, y), Q(x) = (x, x)/2, and L ⊆ V an O_F-lattice. L is even if Q(L) ⊆ 𝔡_F^{−1}, its trace dual is L′ = {y ∈ V : (y, L) ⊆ 𝔡_F^{−1}} (the ℤ-dual of L for Q_ℤ = Tr_{F/ℚ}∘Q), and L is ℤ-unimodular if L′ = L. U_F is the commutative monoid of even ℤ-unimodular lattices under ⊥ and U_F^+ its subsemigroup of nonzero totally positive definite ones. For even L, L′/L is finite with the quadratic form Q mod 𝔡_F^{−1}; for h in the adelic orthogonal (or GSpin) group, L_h = V ∩ h^{−1}L̂ is in the genus of L and the map h^{−1} on finite completed quotients identifies L′/L with L_h′/L_h (after the canonical completion identifications).
hypotheses: F totally real; 𝔡_F^{−1} the inverse different, so Tr_{F/ℚ}(𝔡_F^{−1}) ⊆ ℤ (Mathlib differentIdeal).
proofSteps: L′ = 𝔡_F^{−1}·L^♯ with L^♯ the O_F-dual (lattice-discriminant-ideal), so L′ is a lattice and L′ = L can be checked place by place.
Q_ℤ(L) ⊆ Tr(𝔡_F^{−1}) ⊆ ℤ for even L; L′ is the ℤ-dual of L for the trace form by nondegeneracy of the trace pairing.
L_h is defined through lattice-local-global-dictionary from the completions h^{−1}L̂_v.

Because the discriminant quotients are finite, completion identifies L′/L with the direct sum of its local quotients. Apply h⁻¹ to these completed quotients and use local-global descent for L_h. This does not apply h⁻¹ to a rational vector in V.
acceptance: F = ℚ: even ℤ-unimodular means even unimodular in the usual sense (E₈ ∈ U_ℚ^+).
The hyperbolic plane O_Fe ⊕ 𝔡_F^{−1}f with Q(xe + yf) = xy is in U_F (indefinite).

nodes.title: Existence of definite even ℤ-unimodular lattices over a totally real field
nodes.statement: For every totally real field F and every choice of signs at the real places there is a nonzero even ℤ-unimodular O_F-lattice of rank 8 that is definite with those signs; in particular U_F^+ ≠ ∅.
hypotheses: The rank 8 suffices; ranks divisible by 8 then follow by orthogonal sums.
proofSteps: Choose α ∈ F^× with the prescribed signs (weak approximation) and V = F^8 with Q = α(x_1² + ⋯ + x_8²). At every finite place V_v has dimension 8, square discriminant and trivial Hasse invariant, hence V_v ≅ 4H (QuadraticFormInvariants 6D).

Local lattices: at v ∤ 2𝔡_F with α a v-unit, the standard lattice O_v^8 is even and self-dual for the trace pairing (its polar Gram matrix 2α·I is a unit); at the finitely many other v take ⊕_{i=1}^4 (O_ve_i ⊕ 𝔡_v^{−1}f_i) in 4H, which is even with L_v′ = L_v.
Glue with lattice-local-global-dictionary (the standard lattice at almost all v); evenness and L′ = L are local (trace-unimodular-lattice).
This proof replaces Li's appeal to Chang's existence criterion and to Hecke's theorem that the class of the different is a square; neither is needed.
acceptance: F = ℚ: E₈ (positive signs).
F = ℚ(√2), signs (+, −): a lattice of signature (8, 0) at one real place and (0, 8) at the other.

Its genus contains one class (IntegralLattices 5D, U ⊕ T unique in its genus).

nodes.title: Transport of primitive embeddings into Λ_{2md} (Charles)
nodes.statement: Let d > 0 and S an even positive definite lattice of rank 2 with a primitive embedding S ↪ Λ_{2d}. There are N > 0 and nonzero integers a, b such that for every m > 0 with m ≡ 1 mod N, gcd(m, ab) = 1 and a, b squares modulo m, S admits a primitive embedding into Λ_{2md}. Primitivity of the initial embedding is necessary: in Λ_2 the sublattice spanned by 2h and 2(e + f) is isometric to diag(8, 8) but the abstract lattice diag(8, 8) has no primitive embedding into Λ_2, so the statement for arbitrary rank-2 sublattices fails already at m = 1.
hypotheses: d>0; S even, positive definite of rank two, with a primitive initial embedding. The source correction is PAPER-CHARLES-16/E2, also tracked here as E204.
proofSteps: Nikulin's criterion (IntegralLattices 5I, Proposition 1.15.1): a primitive embedding S ↪ Λ exists iff there are subgroups H_S ⊆ A_S, H ⊆ A_Λ, an isometry γ of the restricted forms and a negative definite rank-one even lattice K = ⟨−2t⟩ with q_K ≅ −δ, δ = (q_S ⊕ −q_Λ)|Γ_γ^⊥/Γ_γ.

Transport the gluing data along id ⊕ m: A_{Λ_{2d}} → A_{Λ_{2md}}; under m ≡ 1 mod 4dt and the coprimality exclusions, the new quotient is cyclic of order 2tm with generator of norm 1/(2t) + y_0²(m − 1)/(2md).

Rescale the generator by λ with λ ≡ 1 mod 4dt and λ²ty_0² + d ≡ 0 mod m, solvable by CRT when −d and t are squares mod m (prime-power-square-lift), giving the cyclic form of ⟨−2tm⟩ and the embedding by 5I.

Counterexample: a primitive embedding of S = diag(8, 8) into Λ_2 has complement K = ⟨−2t⟩ and glue group H, which embeds into both A_S ≅ (ℤ/8)² and A_K ≅ ℤ/2t, so H is cyclic of order at most 8; but |H|² = |A_S||A_K|/|A_{Λ_2}| = 64t forces |H| = 8 and t = 1, contradicting H ⊆ ℤ/2.
acceptance: S with Gram [[2, 1], [1, 2dk²]] is primitively embedded in Λ_{2d} (zarhin-explicit-plane), so the theorem applies to it.

For odd n and k divisible by |n|, l² ≡ −2 mod n, so gcd(l², n) = 1.

proofSteps: Direct computation of the Gram entries with x² = 2da² + 2bc.
Primitivity: the ℤ-linear retraction P(x, y, z) = (z, y − z) of Λ_{2d} onto ℤ² satisfies P(av + bw) = (a, b), so ℤv + ℤw is a direct summand.

nodes.title: Discriminant of the quotient by a primitive isotropic vector
nodes.statement: Let L be a nondegenerate integral ℤ-lattice, v ∈ L primitive and isotropic, and n_v > 0 the generator of (v, L) ⊆ ℤ. Then K = v^⊥/ℤv is a nondegenerate lattice and |disc L| = n_v²·|disc K|.
hypotheses: Integral symmetric bilinear lattice (Tau Ceti IntegralLattice).
proofSteps: Choose w ∈ L with (v, w) = n_v and a basis (w, v, e_1, …, e_r) adapted to v^⊥ = ℤv ⊕ span(e_i) (primitive v); in this basis the Gram matrix has the block form with (w, v) = n_v and (v, v) = (v, e_i) = 0, so det = −n_v²·det(e_i·e_j).

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.3, p.520 (Annals 184)
sources.match: Relates the discriminant of a lattice and of the quotient of the orthogonal of a primitive isotropic vector by the divisibility n_v, via a basis containing v and w with (v, w) = n_v.

nodes.title: Squares modulo ℓ lift; simultaneous quadratic-residue primes
nodes.statement: (a) If ℓ is an odd prime, a ∈ ℤ is prime to ℓ and a square mod ℓ, then a is a square mod ℓ^m for every m ≥ 1. (b) If ℓ is prime to N ≥ 1 then ℓ^{2n} ≡ 1 mod N for infinitely many n (all multiples of the order of ℓ²). (c) For finitely many nonzero integers x_1, …, x_s there are infinitely many primes ℓ such that every x_i is a nonzero square mod ℓ.
hypotheses: ℓ odd in (a); in (c) the excluded finite set of primes dividing some x_i is removed.
proofSteps: (a) Hensel's lemma for X² − a (derivative 2X is a unit at a nonzero root since ℓ is odd).
(b) ℓ ∈ (ℤ/N)^× has finite order (orderOf).

(c) Take ℓ ≡ 1 mod 8 and ℓ ≡ 1 mod every odd prime dividing some x_i; by quadratic reciprocity each such prime and −1, 2 are squares mod ℓ, and Dirichlet's theorem (Nat.infinite_setOfPred_prime_and_eq_mod) gives infinitely many such ℓ.
acceptance: a = 2, ℓ = 7: 2 ≡ 3² mod 7, and 2 is a square mod 49 (10² = 100 ≡ 2).
x = (2, 3, 5): ℓ = 241 ≡ 1 mod 120 makes all three squares.

sources.locator: Lemma 4.6, p.521, and the proof of Theorem 1.3, p.523 (Annals 184)
sources.match: Proves that finitely many integers are simultaneously squares modulo infinitely many primes by reciprocity and Dirichlet, and uses that ℓ^{2n} ≡ 1 mod N along a subsequence with squares lifting to prime powers.

nodes.title: Selecting a vector of prescribed norm in compatible ℓ-adic systems
nodes.statement: For every sufficiently large odd prime ℓ, let M_ℓ be a unimodular ℤ_ℓ-lattice with semisimple isometry φ_ℓ and common characteristic polynomial P∈ℚ[T]; let the determinant of M_ℓ⊗ℚ_ℓ have fixed rational square class δ. Put N_ℓ=M_ℓ∩ker(φ_ℓ²−1), assumed unimodular, and let a fixed nondegenerate integral lattice A embed isometrically as A_ℓ⊆N_ℓ. Suppose T_ℓ=A_ℓ^⊥∩N_ℓ has positive rank. Write P=(T−1)^a(T+1)^bP_* with P_*(±1)≠0. Fix t∈ℚ^×. For infinitely many odd primes ℓ, all of −1, δ, disc A, t and P_*(1)P_*(−1) are nonzero squares in ℚ_ℓ and all relevant coefficients are integral units. At every such sufficiently large prime, T_ℓ contains a vector γ of norm t. It is primitive in A_ℓ^⊥, and γ/ℓ^n has exact order ℓ^n in the torsion group (M_ℓ/A_ℓ)⊗ℚ_ℓ/ℤ_ℓ. No splitting of the full polynomial P over ℚ_ℓ is required.
hypotheses: The finitely many primes dividing the numerators or denominators of the stated rational constants, the denominators of P, or disc A are excluded. Convert each rational square class to a nonzero integer representative for prime-power-square-lift(c).
proofSteps: The orthogonal complement of N_ℓ has no eigenvalues ±1, so the nonsplit Cayley determinant identity makes its determinant square class P_*(1)P_*(−1). Hence disc N_ℓ=δ/(P_*(1)P_*(−1)) modulo squares. A_ℓ is unimodular at these primes and splits integrally, so disc T_ℓ=disc N_ℓ/disc A is a square.

Use prime-power-square-lift(c) and Hensel for the finite list of rational square classes; this gives infinitely many allowed ℓ. If rank T_ℓ≥2, apply odd-unimodular-unit-representation. If its rank is one, its Gram coefficient and t are units with the same square class, so it represents t.

A vector of unit norm cannot lie in ℓ times its lattice. Integral orthogonal splitting makes A_ℓ^⊥ a direct summand of M_ℓ, so its primitivity remains true in M_ℓ/A_ℓ; division by ℓ^n has exact order ℓ^n.
acceptance: P = (T − 1)^r: N_ℓ = M_ℓ and the statement is odd-unimodular-unit-representation for A^⊥.

sources.locator: §3.5, Lemma 3.5.2 and proof, pp.15–16 (arXiv:1107.1221); 3.5.3 is a definition.
sources.match: Supplies the compatible-lattice norm-selection argument. The present version replaces complete splitting by the Cayley determinant identity and finitely many square-class conditions, so the prime supplier really proves what is requested.

sources.locator: §4.2, Lemma 4.5 and its proof, pp.520–521 (Annals 184)
sources.match: Applies this selection to construct twisted partners of K3 surfaces with prescribed Brauer classes.

nodes.title: Discriminants of Frobenius eigenlattices
nodes.statement: Fix r > 0, an even w ≥ 0 and a positive prime power q. Let O be the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_ℓ and M a nondegenerate O-lattice of rank r with an endomorphism φ such that (φx, φy) = q^w(x, y), whose characteristic polynomial lies in ℤ[T] with all roots Weil q-integers of weight w and for which q^{w/2} is a semisimple eigenvalue. Let M_0 = M ∩ ker(φ − q^{w/2}). Then v_ℓ(disc M_0) ≤ v_ℓ(disc M) for ℓ > C(r, w, q), and v_ℓ(disc M_0) ≤ C′(r, w, q) + v_ℓ(disc M) for all ℓ.
hypotheses: The similitude relation (φx, φy) = q^w(x, y) is a hypothesis; the conclusion bounds valuations only, not a rational square class.

The common characteristic polynomial has coefficients in ℤ, not merely in the varying coefficient ring O. All Weil roots have complex absolute value q^{w/2}. The eigenvalue q^{w/2} is semisimple; full semisimplicity is not required.
proofSteps: The fixed degree, integer coefficients and Weil absolute values bound every coefficient by a binomial expression, giving a finite set of polynomials. Factor each as g_i=(T−q^{w/2})^{a_i} and h_i with h_i(q^{w/2})≠0. Clear denominators in Bézout identities a_i g_i+b_i h_i=1 using a single positive integer Q. Take C at least the largest prime factor of Q and C′=2r·max_ℓ v_ℓ(Q), an integer independent of ℓ.

The similitude relation makes the q^{w/2}-eigenspace orthogonal to the other primary summands: their eigenvalues cannot pair to q^w with q^{w/2}. Semisimplicity of this eigenvalue ensures h_i(φ)M⊆M_0. For ℓ∤Q the Bézout projector is integral and gives M=M_0⊥M_2, so the integral complementary determinant has nonnegative valuation. In general ℓ^{v_ℓ(Q)}M⊆h_i(φ)M⊕g_i(φ)M; its index has length ≤r v_ℓ(Q). The index-square discriminant formula then bounds v_ℓ(disc M_0) by v_ℓ(disc M)+2r v_ℓ(Q).
acceptance: φ = q^{w/2}·id: M_0 = M and the bound is equality.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.1.2 and its proof, pp.3–4 (arXiv:1107.1221)
sources.match: Bounds the discriminant valuation of the q^{w/2}-eigenlattice of a lattice with a Frobenius-type similitude in terms of that of the ambient lattice, uniformly for large ℓ.

sources.locator: Proof of Lemma 4.5, p.520 (Annals 184)
sources.match: Uses the Lieblich–Maulik–Snowden bound to control the discriminant of Néron–Severi-type eigenlattices.

nodes.title: Signatures split off the Witt group of a Dedekind ring
nodes.statement: Let R be a Dedekind domain with global fraction field K of characteristic ≠2. Use symmetric bilinear Witt groups and an invertible coefficient module M with +1 involution. If K is nonreal, W(K) is 2-primary torsion of bounded exponent (indeed killed by 8). If K has a real embedding σ, the untwisted signature W(R)→W(ℝ)≅ℤ is onto and splits by ⟨1⟩. For line-valued coefficients, choose a trivialization M⊗K≅K. The comparison W(R;M)[1/2]→W(K)[1/2] is an isomorphism; hence the signature composite is nonzero, with image dℤ for some d>0. Choosing a preimage of d splits the surjection onto dℤ≅ℤ, so ℤ is a direct summand of W(R;M). In particular it is not 2-adically complete. Surjectivity onto the chosen signature ℤ is not asserted for arbitrary M, and alternating (−1) coefficients are excluded.
hypotheses: The Witt group is the classical group of nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms on finite projective modules, with values in M. The line coefficient has +1 involution. The L-theory consequences belong to Layer 6.
The line-valued comparison after inverting 2 is a named source input, with its localization proof recorded as a gap rather than inferred from a generator at one real place.
proofSteps: For nonreal K, the global-to-local Witt map is injective and each nonarchimedean or complex local Witt group is killed by 8; therefore so is W(K).

For real σ and M=R, the class ⟨1⟩ maps to signature 1 and gives an explicit section. For general M, use the localization comparison after inverting 2 stated in Calmès et al. Remark 3.1.9; signature on W(K)[1/2] is onto ℤ[1/2], so the composite cannot be zero. Its nonzero subgroup of ℤ is dℤ. Lift d and extend by integer multiples to split onto this image, which is abstractly ℤ.

A direct summand ℤ prevents 2-adic completeness, since its completion is ℤ₂ and the natural map ℤ→ℤ₂ is not onto. The exact line-valued localization theorem required for the second step is listed in gaps.
acceptance: K = ℚ(i): ⟨1⟩ ⊥ ⟨1⟩ is hyperbolic since −1 is a square, so ⟨1⟩ has order 2 in W(K).
R = ℤ: W(ℤ) ≅ ℤ by the signature, and E₈ has signature 8.

sources.match: Notes that for nonreal global K the Witt group is 2-primary torsion of bounded exponent, making L^s(R) 2-complete, while a real embedding makes ℤ a direct summand of W^s(R; M), so the comparison of Theorem 3.1.7 is not an integral equivalence.

nodes.title: Integral ternary forms with half-discriminant ±1
nodes.statement: Every integral ternary quadratic form f(x, y, z) = Σ a_{ij}x_ix_j over ℤ (cross terms with arbitrary integer coefficients) whose half-discriminant 4·det(A_f) is −1, with A_f the half-integral Gram matrix (A_f)_{ii} = a_{ii}, (A_f)_{ij} = a_{ij}/2, is GL₃(ℤ)-equivalent to y² − xz; those with 4det A_f = +1 are equivalent to xz − y². In particular such forms are indefinite, isotropic over ℚ and form a single class (up to sign).
hypotheses: Integral means integer coefficients a_{ij}; the half-discriminant convention 4det(A_f) is the one of Bhargava and Wood for ternary forms.
proofSteps: For odd p, the polar Gram determinant is 8det A_f=±2, hence a unit; finite-field classification gives a nonzero isotropic vector and perfect polarization makes it smooth. At p=2 the reduction is a regular ternary form with a one-dimensional polar radical, and q is nonzero on that line. The characteristic-two result of finite-field-quadratic-classification gives a nonzero isotropic vector outside the radical, hence a smooth zero. Hensel lifts these vectors to ℚ_p-isotropy.

If f or −f were positive definite, its integer minimum would be at least 1. IntegralLattices 2E gives min f≤(4/3)(det A_f)^{1/3}=(4/3)(1/4)^{1/3}<1, a contradiction. Thus f is indefinite and isotropic over ℝ; Hasse–Minkowski gives a rational isotropic vector. Clear denominators and divide by the coordinate gcd to obtain a primitive v∈ℤ³.

The ideal b(v,L) is ℤ. At odd p, unimodularity and v primitive imply it has a unit value. At 2, v mod2 is a nonzero isotropic vector and cannot be in the radical, so again a unit value occurs. Choose w with b(v,w)=1 and replace w by w−q(w)v, making q(w)=0. The span of v,w is an integral hyperbolic plane and splits because its polar determinant is −1.

The orthogonal rank-one complement has q(z)=az² for a∈ℤ. Its polar determinant is 2a, so 8det A_f=−2a forces a=−1 when 4det A_f=+1 and a=1 when 4det A_f=−1. Therefore f is equivalent to xy−z² or xy+z², and a permutation/sign change gives exactly the two stated models.
acceptance: For f=xy+yz+zx, 4det A_f=+1. The unimodular change X=x+y, Y=y, Z=y+z has f=XZ−Y², exhibiting the required model and determinant-one change directly.

sources.locator: Section 3.2, the definition of regular quadratic forms in odd rank through the half-discriminant, p.28 (arXiv:1907.08783)
sources.match: Defines regularity of an odd-rank quadratic form over a ring by the invertibility of its half-discriminant, the condition 4det = ±1 here.
